environment_overhead_note: Input token counts are dominated by the installed session skill/plugin catalog and cache variance; per-run deltas are not attributable to the lesson.
lesson_scoping: The lesson concerns denominator cancellation. The fixture's claim cancels (x - 1) without stating x != 1, so the lesson is genuinely in scope. The lesson-assisted run explicitly judged the lesson in scope ("matches and was applied"), validated it, stated the missing x != 1 denominator assumption, and recommended re-verification under the corrected domain.
limitations: Single model, single reasoning effort, one in-scope fixture, one run per condition; not a model-accuracy benchmark.

Both runs judged FAILED: the baseline via a boundary counterexample at x = 1; the lesson-assisted run additionally invoked the approved lesson and named the missing denominator assumption. The lesson's demonstrated effect is qualitative (explicit rule application and assumption naming), not a verdict change.

The SymPy residual of (x^2 - 1)/(x - 1) - (x + 1) simplifies to 0 (PASS), which would falsely verify the universal claim; the fixture deliberately carries no residual field because the defect is a missing domain assumption, which residual simplification cannot detect. Both runs correctly did not treat the CAS PASS as establishing the universal claim.
